title: Headless E-Commerce Platform with Optimistic UI & Atomic Inventory Locks
problem: Modern e-commerce web applications must deliver instantaneous client-side interactions while guaranteeing strict backend data consistency during high-concurrency flash sales. Naive implementations suffer from sluggish shopping cart state synchronizations and inventory overselling when multiple shoppers purchase the final item simultaneously. This project builds a high-performance headless e-commerce platform in Next.js, React, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Prisma, and Stripe. The system implements optimistic client-side UI updates for seamless cart interactions, transactional database row locking to prevent overselling, resilient Stripe checkout session creation with idempotent webhook fulfillment, and server-side rendered (SSR) catalog pages with stale-while-revalidate caching.
use_cases: High-volume consumer retail storefronts requiring zero overselling during limited product drops
Digital goods marketplaces delivering instant checkout workflows with automated webhook fulfillment
Headless commerce frontends decoupling customized customer experiences from backend catalog databases
hard_parts: Preventing inventory overselling race conditions across concurrent checkouts via PostgreSQL SELECT FOR UPDATE locks
Managing optimistic shopping cart UI updates with automatic rollback when backend validation rejects changes
Processing asynchronous Stripe payment webhooks idempotently to eliminate duplicate order creation
Coordinating server-side catalog caching and on-demand revalidation to ensure price accuracy
screener_signals: Clean TypeScript codebase cleanly separating Next.js app routes, Prisma schemas, cart state machines, and Stripe webhooks
Automated flash-sale stress test simulating 100 concurrent checkouts on a single inventory item without overselling
Anti-fake verification script creating dynamic product SKUs, launching concurrent purchase requests, and asserting lock integrity

components.purpose: Initializes Stripe checkout sessions and processes charge.succeeded webhooks idempotently

architecture.data_flow: Shoppers browse SSR product pages served by Next.js; adding items immediately triggers optimistic React state updates; upon proceeding to checkout, the backend executes an atomic Prisma transaction that locks inventory rows using PostgreSQL SELECT FOR UPDATE; if stock is available, inventory reserves and a Stripe checkout session is generated; customer completes payment on Stripe; Stripe posts a webhook event to Next.js API; the webhook handler checks event idempotency in PostgreSQL, marks the order PAID, and finalizes stock deduction.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: PostgreSQL transactional row-level locks preventing simultaneous double-allocation of limited stock; Stripe webhook signature verification.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: a headless e-commerce platform in Next.js/React with Prisma, PostgreSQL row locks, and idempotent Stripe webhooks.
worksheet.q2: Target users: full-stack developers, frontend platform engineers, and e-commerce architects.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: flash sale consumer retail, digital goods marketplaces, and headless commerce frontends.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 28 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 24 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 27.6 -> 28 hours. Intermediate level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: transactional row locking with SELECT FOR UPDATE, optimistic cart rollbacks, idempotent Stripe webhooks, and SSR catalog caching.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 250 product SKUs across 10 categories with 10,000 synthetic inventory stock units. Mock test data only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, free Stripe test account. Fallback: SQLite and mock payment gateway.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: Deadlocks under high-concurrency locking. Fallback: consistent ascending SKU sorting before acquiring locks.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: mock cart returns without database locking. Anti-fake check 5 provisions dynamic SKU with 1 stock, runs 10 concurrent checkouts, and asserts exactly 1 succeeds.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; synthetic products and Stripe test credit card tokens only.
